Write the Round Machine — setup_round()

Create a function that loads the right picture and answers for each round

What we're doing: A function is like a recipe. We write it once, then "call" it whenever we need a fresh round. This function loads the right picture, fills the four answer buttons with text, and updates the round counter.

🧩 Analogy Think of setup_round() as a vending machine. You press the button (call the function), and it drops out a perfectly set-up round — correct image, correct answers, correct labels. No matter which round you're on, it always delivers the right thing.

Create the Function

  1. Open Functions in the toolbox
  2. Drag a define setup_round() block into Setup (after your lists). No parameters needed.

Inside the function body, add these blocks:

a) Set the Image

  1. From M5UI, find Set quiz_image local image (auto-generated when you closed the UI Editor)
  2. For the source value, use Lists → in list get #. Set the list to images and the index to current_round:
    Set quiz_image local image in list images get # current_round
💡 Why current_round works directly Since current_round starts at 1, we can use it directly to grab the right picture! When round = 1, we get Q1.jpg. When round = 5, we get Q5.jpg. No offsets, no confusion.

b) Get the Answers for This Round

  1. First, we need a new variable to hold the 4 answers for the current round. Create a variable called current_choices.
  2. Drag set current_choices to value into the function body (before setting the button texts).
  3. Set it to: Lists → in list get # from all_answers at index current_round
    set current_choices to in list all_answers get # current_round

This grabs the whole sub-list for this round from the bookshelf! If current_round is 3, current_choices becomes ["Statue of Liberty", "Tower of Pisa", "Big Ben", "Eiffel Tower"].

c) Set the Four Answer Buttons

  1. Find Set answer_btn1 text to from M5UI. For the text: Lists → in list current_choices get # 1
  2. Same for answer_btn2: Lists → in list current_choices get # 2
  3. Same for answer_btn3: Lists → in list current_choices get # 3
  4. Same for answer_btn4: Lists → in list current_choices get # 4

d) Update the Round Label

  1. Find Set round_label text to from M5UI
  2. UIFlow2 has no join block — use nested Text → [] + [] blocks:
    • First, current_round
    • Inner [] + []: current_round + "/8"
    • Outer [] + []: "Round: " + (inner result)
✅ What you should see: Your define setup_round() function now contains: an image loader, a current_choices variable setter, four button text setters, and a round label updater. That's your round machine — ready to go!
💾 Save your progress! Your function can now load any round! Next we'll write the judge that checks answers.
📋 Complete Function — Here's What setup_round() Should Look Like

When you're done, your function should look like this:

define setup_round()
Set quiz_image local image → in list images get # current_round
set current_choices to → in list all_answers get # current_round
Set answer_btn1 text to → in list current_choices get # 1
Set answer_btn2 text to → in list current_choices get # 2
Set answer_btn3 text to → in list current_choices get # 3
Set answer_btn4 text to → in list current_choices get # 4
Set round_label text to → ["Round: " + (current_round + "/8")]
